headline: Cowork Chat is the product's collaborative AI workspace — chat with streaming replies, file deliverables, a code agent, a terminal and an output view — and of its 11 tickets the code review could back up 3 (streaming chat, auto-saved file deliverables, and stop/cancel), while the other 8 could not be confirmed either way from the files examined.
what_is_there: The backend of the Cowork conversation is visibly built: messages stream back incrementally, history is retained, the agent can save real files (spreadsheets, documents, slides, markdown) into an output folder and tidy away intermediate drafts, and there is working plumbing to cancel a running turn. Sandbox and safety policy for code execution exists as configuration.
what_is_unclear: Almost everything that lives in the on-screen interface — the message composer with attachments, per-tab model picker and skill attachment, the file output tree, the terminal panel — was not part of the files the analysis read, so it could not be confirmed or ruled out. The code agent's file read/write/edit tools, the sandboxed code runner, multi-file revision, and the in-progress 'Superpowers' item are likewise unsettled rather than shown to be absent.
suggested_action: Ask the team to point the analysis at the Cowork tab interface code and the code-agent/runner implementation, then re-run the check so the eight open questions can be resolved.
caveat: One sandbox configuration setting blocks code generation in Cowork mode and a rulebook forbids the Cowork agent from coding tasks, which sits oddly beside a 'Cowork Chat code runner' ticket — though a separate Code agent appears to exist, so this may simply be a naming overlap worth confirming.
